chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from Jamil from 'Abd al-Rahman and Muhammad ibn Humran, all of them, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The minimum amount in which the thief's hand is cut off is five dinars.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum value of stolen goods required for hadd punishment in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the nisab for hadd al-sariqah at five dinars, reflecting the Umayyad-era gold standard where a dinar weighed approximately 4.25 grams. In Shia jurisprudence, this narration is pivotal for determining the minimum value of stolen goods required to trigger the specific corporal punishment, emphasizing the precision of monetary valuation in legal rulings.
